issues.legal_issue: A civil court lacks jurisdiction over a challenge to the legality of a Panchayat lease when a statutory authority is empowered to determine the challenge and the lease is not a nullity.
material_facts: The suit sought a declaration that a Panchayat lease was invalid and an injunction against activities on the leased land.
The plaintiffs alleged that the lease violated the governing rules, including because its term exceeded the permitted duration and the auction notices did not comply with notice requirements.

The statute empowered a revenue authority to examine the legality of Panchayat leases and to cancel or vary a lease entered into in violation of the statute or its rules, through a process requiring a hearing for the parties.
The Court considered that the lease might be illegal but was not a nullity.
issues.conclusion: The civil court had no jurisdiction to entertain and adjudicate the challenge. The appeal was allowed, the lower appellate judgments were set aside, and the trial court’s dismissal of the suit for want of jurisdiction was restored. The plaintiffs remained free to seek relief from the appropriate statutory authority.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure, civil courts may try suits of a civil nature unless their jurisdiction is expressly or impliedly barred. The exclusion of civil jurisdiction is construed strictly. Under the principles in M/s. Kamala Mills Ltd. v. State of Bombay and Lala Ram Swarup v. Shikar Chand, an implied bar is assessed by considering the statutory scheme and whether an adequate and effective alternative remedy exists; even where jurisdiction is barred, a civil court may entertain a challenge to an order that is a nullity. Section 13 of the Punjab Village Common Lands (Regulation) Act, 1961 bars civil-court jurisdiction over matters assigned to revenue authorities, and Section 10-A empowers the Assistant Collector of the First Grade to examine and cancel or vary a Panchayat lease on grounds including violation of the Act or rules, fraud, or detriment to the Panchayat. The Court also referred to Babu Ram v. Gram Sabha Bahavi concerning the bar applicable to claims within Section 13(a)(i). Here, the alleged lease irregularities were matters for the authority under Section 10-A, and the lease was not a nullity.

predicates.civil_suit_challenges_public_body_lease_: A claimant brought a civil suit challenging the validity of a lease granted by a public body.
predicates.special_authority_can_review_lease_legal: A specially empowered authority can examine and grant relief concerning the legality of that kind of lease.
predicates.challenge_concerns_grounds_within_that_a: The challenge relies on grounds that the specially empowered authority is authorized to determine.
predicates.challenged_transaction_is_not_a_nullity: The challenged transaction may be unlawful but is not a nullity.

issues.definition: When a civil suit challenges a public body's lease on grounds a specially empowered authority can determine, and the challenged transaction is not a nullity, civil-court jurisdiction is barred.
